name: Cashio
rootCause: $48M CASHed out. The latest leaderboard entry comes from the Solana network, where an anonymous attacker used an infinite mint to make Cashio print faster than the Fed.

descriptions.text: $48M CASHed out. The latest leaderboard entry comes from the Solana network, where an anonymous attacker used an infinite mint to make Cashio print faster than the Fed.

The stablecoin project Cashio on Solana has been hacked. According to the preliminary analysis of the SlowMist security team, hackers illegally issued 2 billion CASH tokens by bypassing an unverified account, and converted CASH tokens into 8,646,022.04 UST, 17,041,006.5 USDC and 26,340,965.68 USDT-USDC through multiple applications. LP, total profit value: 52027994.22 USD (more than 50 million USD). At present, the official announcement has been issued to allow users to suspend the use of the contract, and a temporary patch has been released to fix the vulnerability.

On March 23, 2022, Cashio on Solana suffered a loss of about $52.8 million after an attacker forged a chain of fake accounts to bypass collateral ownership checks, enabling infinite unbacked minting of the CASH stablecoin. The attacker swapped these tokens for real stablecoins, collapsing CASH's value and draining protocol reserves. Cashio's minting logic failed to verify program ownership for each account in the collateral chain, specifically omitting the check for the intermediate 'arrow' collateral account. This allowed an attacker to supply a counterfeit account and mint unlimited unbacked CASH tokens.
